why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.

proof_points.claim: Rapido is India's fastest-rising platform with a multi-format DNA.
proof_points.evidence: From a Bengaluru bike-taxi network, Rapido surged into autos and cabs to become Uber's primary rival, taking 20%+ four-wheeler share since entering the segment. Adding a water format fits a platform built to add formats fast.

proof_points.claim: The vessel is commercial today.
proof_points.evidence: The N30 Pioneer II is in commercial service now — 70 nm range, ~30 kt, 6–8 passengers — already operating with the Four Seasons on Lake Austin. Delivery-ready, not a concept.

proof_points.claim: A network at scale is already being built in the region.
proof_points.evidence: Navier is ramping a roughly 100-vessel water network in the Maldives with JIH Global over three years and signed a national agreement with WorldBridge in Cambodia in May 2026.

proof_points.claim: A water format is differentiated demand off the road price war.
proof_points.evidence: Hydrofoiling's low energy per passenger-mile lets a value-led platform offer a faster water option that a road-only rival can't match on time — new demand, not a fare fight.

objections.concern: We compete hard on price — is a water tier affordable enough?
objections.response: Foiling's efficiency is exactly what makes an affordable water format possible. The harbour crossing or backwater run isn't a luxury — it replaces hours of gridlock, and Rapido's value-led model is the right home for it.

objections.concern: Is the range enough for India's coast?
objections.response: The dense commute and bay hops — Mumbai↔Alibaug ~11 nm, Panaji↔beaches ~14 nm — sit inside the all-electric Pioneer II envelope, and the Quanta-LR hybrid reaches the Andamans with no charging infrastructure required.

objections.concern: Adding a wholly new mode is a big step.
objections.response: Rapido already proved it can add formats fast — bikes to autos to cabs. Water is the next format, and you don't build or run the fleet: Navier brings vessels, captains and maintenance; you bring demand, dispatch and the app.

objections.concern: India's marine infrastructure is uneven.
objections.response: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists — open water and jetties already in use. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal, so launch doesn't wait on new ports.

end_state.headline: The water format of India's fastest-rising mobility platform.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every coastal and backwater market Rapido already serves — Mumbai and the Konkan, Goa's rivers and coast, Kerala's Kochi and backwaters, the Andaman & Nicobar islands, Kolkata/Hooghly and Chennai/ECR.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is the coastal map of India as a new Rapido format. Start where the congestion is worst — Mumbai's harbour, Goa's coast — prove the water format, then scale it the way Rapido scaled bikes, autos and cabs.
